# react-threaded — full LLM context

> Typed Web Workers for React: React hooks, hard cancellation, worker pools, shared atomics, plugins, and Comlink-style method proxies. Zero runtime dependencies.

Canonical site: https://hussain-ahmed2.github.io/react-threaded/
Source: https://github.com/hussain-ahmed2/react-threaded
Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-threaded
License: MIT

## What it is

react-threaded runs typed functions in browser Web Workers. The runtime and handler are serialized into a Blob URL, so consumers do not create a separate worker entry file and there is no worker MIME or bundler path to configure.

Main features:

- `createWorker` for a typed one-method worker.
- `useWorker` for React state, progress, results, errors, and cancellation.
- `cancel({ mode: 'terminate' })` for immediate hard cancellation.
- `cancel({ mode: 'cooperative' })` for task-defined checkpoints.
- `useWorkerPool` for bounded fan-out and backpressure.
- `createSharedAtom` and `useSharedAtom` for cross-worker atomic counters.
- `createWorker` method maps and `useWorkerProxy` for typed multi-method workers.
- Plugin hooks for retry, logging, timing, and lifecycle behavior.
- Structured-clone-safe transferables for ownership transfer.
- Full TypeScript inference for input, output, progress, and errors.

## Requirements

- React 18 or newer.
- TypeScript 5 or newer for the best inference.
- A modern browser with Web Workers.
- HTTPS or localhost for production and local development.
- Cross-origin isolation only for `SharedArrayBuffer` and shared atoms.

## Execution and memory contract

- A worker function must be self-contained. It cannot close over module state or call imported functions unless those values are passed in.
- Inputs and outputs cross a structured-clone boundary. Functions, DOM nodes, class instances without clone support, and React elements cannot be sent.
- `ArrayBuffer` can be copied or transferred. Transferring detaches the sender's buffer.
- Cancellation in terminate mode destroys the current worker and respawns it on the next run.
- Shared atoms use a `SharedArrayBuffer` plus `Atomics`. They require cross-origin isolation.
- A shared atom falls back to local mode when isolation is unavailable.
- Inline Blob workers require CSP `worker-src blob:`. `unsafe-eval` is not required.
- Use worker hooks only in Client Components or client-only React islands. Server rendering cannot create a Worker.

## Cross-origin isolation

Required response headers for shared memory:

```
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp
```

Verify:

```js
console.log({ isolated: crossOriginIsolated, sab: typeof SharedArrayBuffer })
```

COEP `require-corp` blocks third-party resources that do not opt in with CORP or CORS. If shared memory is not needed, omit both headers.

GitHub Pages cannot set response headers. It always reports `crossOriginIsolated === false`.

## Deployment compatibility matrix

| Framework | Vercel | Netlify | Cloudflare | GitHub Pages |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Next.js | Native server | Server adapter (OpenNext) | Server adapter (OpenNext; vinext is the new-project path) | Static export only |
| React Router framework mode | Server adapter (`@vercel/react-router`) | Server adapter (`@netlify/vite-plugin-react-router`) | Server adapter (Cloudflare Vite plugin) | Static SPA only |
| React + Vite | Static | Static | Static | Static |
| Astro | Static or adapter | Static or adapter | Static or adapter | Static only |
| TanStack Start | Server adapter (Nitro) | Server adapter (Netlify plugin) | Server adapter (Cloudflare Vite plugin) | Static SPA only |
| Waku | Server adapter | Server adapter | Server adapter | Static only, no SPA fallback |
| RedwoodSDK | Not supported | Not supported | Native Workers | Not supported |
| Gatsby | Static | Static | Static | Static only |

## Routing rules

- A catch-all rewrite `/* -> /index.html` is correct only for client-rendered apps.
- Vite React apps and React Router SPA mode need a rewrite or `404.html` fallback for deep links.
- Next.js, Waku, RedwoodSDK, TanStack Start server mode, and React Router framework mode must not receive a blanket static rewrite.
- Static exports can use generated per-route HTML shells and a `404.html`.
- GitHub project pages need a base path such as `/repository-name/` in both the bundler and the router.
- GitHub Pages serves a directory `index.html` for paths with a trailing slash.
- A static SPA fallback on GitHub Pages is a `404.html` file that boots the app.

## Framework notes

### Next.js

- Put all worker hooks in files with `'use client'`.
- Do not call worker hooks in Server Components.
- Define COOP/COEP in `next.config.ts` with `headers()`.
- Netlify: publish `.next`; Netlify installs its current OpenNext adapter automatically.
- Netlify: do not add `/* -> /index.html` and do not pin an old adapter plugin.
- Vercel: native Next.js runtime; do not add an SPA rewrite.
- Cloudflare: use `@opennextjs/cloudflare`; Cloudflare recommends vinext for new Next.js projects.
- GitHub Pages: use `output: 'export'`, `images.unoptimized`, and `basePath` from `PAGES_BASE_PATH`; `headers()` and rewrites are ignored.

### React Router

- SPA mode uses `ssr: false`; framework mode uses `ssr: true`.
- Vercel preset: `@vercel/react-router/vite` with `vercelPreset()`.
- Netlify: `@netlify/vite-plugin-react-router`.
- Cloudflare: `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`; React Router v7 needs the unstable Vite environment API; SPA mode and prerender are not supported through this plugin.
- GitHub Pages: set Vite `base`, React Router `basename`, and copy `index.html` to `404.html`.

### React + Vite

- Vite `server.headers` and `preview.headers` cover local development only.
- Static hosts need the headers repeated in `vercel.json`, `netlify.toml`, or `_headers`.
- Vercel and Netlify use a rewrite for BrowserRouter deep links.
- Cloudflare Pages uses `_redirects`.
- GitHub Pages uses a `404.html` shell and has no custom headers.

### Astro

- Static by default.
- Add `@astrojs/vercel`, `@astrojs/netlify`, or `@astrojs/cloudflare` only for on-demand rendering.
- Islands that own workers need `client:load` or another client directive.
- Top-level `server.headers` covers dev and preview; production hosts need their own header configuration.
- GitHub Pages can only host static output.

### TanStack Start

- Default output is a server application.
- Vercel uses Nitro.
- Netlify uses `@netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start`.
- Cloudflare uses `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` and `main: "@tanstack/react-start/server-entry"`.
- GitHub Pages requires SPA mode and `_shell.html` served as `404.html`.

### Waku

- Waku is a React Server Components framework.
- Server adapters: `waku/adapters/vercel`, `waku/adapters/netlify`, `waku/adapters/cloudflare`.
- Netlify builds with `NETLIFY=1`.
- Cloudflare builds with `CLOUDFLARE=1`, outputs `dist/worker.js`, and serves `dist/public`.
- Fully static output lives in `dist/public`.
- GitHub Pages can host only the static output and must not use an SPA fallback.

### RedwoodSDK

- RedwoodSDK is Cloudflare Workers only.
- Use Cloudflare Workers and `pnpm release` or Wrangler.
- Vercel, Netlify, and GitHub Pages are not supported deployment targets.

### Gatsby

- Static output lives in `public`.
- No SPA catch-all rewrite is required.
- GitHub Pages uses `pathPrefix` and `gatsby build --prefix-paths`.
- GitHub Pages cannot set COOP or COEP.

## API surface

Import from `react-threaded`:

- `createWorker`
- `useWorker`
- `createWorkerPool`
- `useWorkerPool`
- `createSharedAtom`
- `useSharedAtom`
- `useWorkerProxy`
- `isSharedMemoryAvailable`
- Worker error classes and public types

`useWorker` accepts `autoRun` for one typed initial task on mount. Use `input` for a
single-function worker and `method` plus `args` for a methods worker. Parent renders and
subsequent `autoRun` value changes do not start another task; call `run` or `call` for
later work.

Refer to the API page for exact signatures and examples:

https://hussain-ahmed2.github.io/react-threaded/docs/api

## Common failure causes

- `SharedArrayBuffer is not defined`: the document is not cross-origin isolated, or the browser or host does not provide SAB. Use COOP/COEP or the local atom fallback.
- Worker creation blocked: CSP does not allow `worker-src blob:`.
- Deep link returns 404: missing SPA fallback or framework server route.
- Server render crashes: a worker hook ran during SSR or in a Server Component.
- Data clone error: the payload contains a function, DOM node, or unsupported class instance.
- Worker function fails at runtime: it closes over module state or calls an import that is not available inside the Blob worker.
- Headers work in dev but not production: the framework dev server applied them, but the static host did not.
- GitHub Pages deep link works only from the home page: missing base path, missing `404.html`, or the router basename does not match the repository path.

## Source layout

- `packages/react-threaded`: library source, tests, and package build.
- `apps/demo`: Vite React demo, documentation site, playground, static SEO assets, and Pages build script.
- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`: verification, build, and GitHub Pages deployment.
